QUOTE: The guard is for application developers and their code... `#ifndef MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS #define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) private_##member #else #define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) member`; "by default a field `foo` is actually named `private_foo`"; "The library and the two sample programs are the only code that gets to write `ctx->foo` directly."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer shows both branches of the macro and says that code defining the opt-out sees plain names, while ordinary consumers of the headers see the `private_` names and must go through `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE` or accessors.
